patterns_data.top_pattern: ME authorized acute hospital admissions surged in HMO
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: ME Commercial Individual HMO acute hospital admissions with PA required
patterns_data.pattern_details: ME HMO acute hospital spend increased primarily because authorized admissions rose sharply, not because hospital price per admission increased. The increase was concentrated in acute hospital inpatient activity, while paid and allowed per admit both moved down. This is a utilization issue first, with authorization workflow alignment as a secondary check.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A large admission spike can overwhelm medical management savings even when unit cost trends are favorable.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch a ME-focused utilization and authorization review for HMO acute hospital admissions, including admission appropriateness, repeat admission patterns, and any changes in referral or authorization behavior.
evidence_summary: ME HMO acute hospital spend increased about $26.0M.
Admissions increased by 676 and claims increased by 352.
Average paid per admit fell by about $35.0K, showing the increase was volume-led rather than price-led.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Auth coding and facility mapping shifts must be fixed before acting on several trends
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Authorization classification and facility mapping across CT, GA, CA, CO, ME, WI, and IN
patterns_data.pattern_details: Several large changes appear tied to authorization-code distribution shifts or facility records falling into Not Mapped rather than to a clean change in utilization or reimbursement. CT and GA have major authorization classification movement, and additional spend is sitting in Not Mapped facility buckets in ME, CT, CA, and IN. Business actions on UM or reimbursement should wait until these classifications are reconciled.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Misclassified authorization or facility data can send the business to the wrong intervention and distort measured savings or leakage.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Reconcile PA-required coding and remap Not Mapped facilities before changing UM rules, provider actions, or reimbursement strategy in the affected segments.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Large AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION shifts and Not Mapped facility values can reclassify spend without reflecting a true underlying utilization or reimbursement change.

GA authorization classification movement affected about $6.4M, led by WELLSTAR MCG HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER and EMORY SAINT JOSEPH'S HOSPITAL.
A separate multi-state authorization distribution issue touched about $3.3M of absolute change across CA, CO, ME, and WI.
Not Mapped facility buckets added about $2.7M across ME, CT, CA, and IN.

patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Route these cases to oncology clinical and UM review to confirm inpatient appropriateness, evaluate outpatient site-of-care alternatives where appropriate, and assess reimbursement policy for CAR-T and inpatient chemotherapy episodes.

patterns_data.why_it_matters: Maternity episodes recur at scale, so even moderate acuity shifts can create sustained cost pressure if care pathways do not change.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Have maternity clinical and UM teams review higher-acuity vaginal delivery admissions in TX, including complication coding, obstetric care pathways, and provider-specific practice variation.
evidence_summary: TX higher-acuity maternity episodes added about $1.6M.
Gestational diabetes during childbirth added about $271K on 10 admissions.
Preterm labor and delivery added about $258K on 6 admissions, and mild to moderate pre-eclampsia added about $204K on 6 admissions.
Post-term pregnancy added about $207K on 26 admissions, pointing to additional volume as well as acuity.

rows.ob_global_billing: BCBS_TX bundles routine OB care/delivery globally; supported complications bill separately; prolonged services not reimbursed.
rows.cesarean_doc_rules: Documentation must justify all billed services, extra antepartum visits, and separately coded complications.

rows.ob_global_billing: Transvaginal ultrasound primary; concurrent transabdominal ultrasound may be reimbursed at 50%.
rows.cesarean_doc_rules: No specific cesarean documentation rules stated.

rows.ob_global_billing: Cigna bundles routine OB services globally; separate billing only for partial care or qualifying complications.
rows.cesarean_doc_rules: Require documentation of obstetric care components, complication visits, and multiple gestation support for modifier 22.

rows.ob_global_billing: Multiple-birth vaginal deliveries pay 50%; delivery sterilization follows multiple surgery rules, otherwise not separate.
rows.cesarean_doc_rules: Requires standard coding support and signed state-approved informed consent documentation.

rows.ob_global_billing: Global OB allowed only under same provider/TIN; otherwise bill components; routine pregnancy E/M included.
rows.cesarean_doc_rules: Medical records must support services; submit modifier 22 documentation and global antepartum, delivery, postpartum records.

rows.ob_global_billing: Moda bundles vaginal delivery complication management into global OB; medically necessary high-risk antepartum visits separate.
rows.cesarean_doc_rules: Support separate high-risk antepartum billing; quantify extra complexity in operative report and appeal.

rows.ob_global_billing: Global OB bundled; Texas requires non-global delivery/postpartum billing, with modifier 22 for severe lacerations.
rows.cesarean_doc_rules: Modifier 22 requires supporting records; high-risk complications need diagnosis coding at delivery.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Post-acute and alternative site-of-care spending is rising across rehab, SNF, LTCH, children's, and critical access settings
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Physical Rehab, SNF - FREE STANDING, LONG TERM CARE HOSPITAL, CHILDRENS, and CRITICAL ACCESS settings
patterns_data.pattern_details: Spending is increasing across several non-acute and alternative facility settings, especially Physical Rehab, with additional pressure in SNF, LTCH, children's hospitals, and critical access facilities. The spread across products and states suggests a site-of-care and discharge-destination issue rather than a single provider event. This pattern should be addressed through steerage, discharge planning, and contract review by setting.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: When patients shift into higher-cost downstream settings, total episode cost rises even if the initial acute stay does not.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review discharge destination patterns, admission criteria, and contracted rates for rehab, SNF, LTCH, children's, and critical access settings, and tighten site-of-care steerage where clinically appropriate.
evidence_summary: These site-of-care settings added about $2.3M in total.
CA EPO Physical Rehab added about $0.5M on 10 admissions, with about $50.3K higher paid per admit.
A multi-state HMO Physical Rehab cluster across CA, CO, IN, and VA added about $0.3M, led by CA and VA.
TX added about $0.3M in HMO Physical Rehab and about $0.2M in Critical Access, while CA SNF, LTCH, and Children's settings together added roughly $0.6M.
